detailed_results.question: How do you perform a factory reset on the Archer D7?
detailed_results.expected:
To reset the modem router to factory default settings:  
1. Visit http://tplinkmodem.net, and log in with the password you set for the modem router.  
2. Click Advanced > System Tools > Backup & Restore page.  
3. Click Factory Restore to reset the modem router.  
4. Wait for the resetting and then the modem router will automatically reboot.  
Note:  
1. During the resetting process, do not turn off or reset the modem router.  
2. We strongly recommend you back up the current configuration settings before resetting the modem router.
detailed_results.generated:
1. Ensure the Archer D7 is powered on.  
2. Press and hold the WPS/RESET button on the rear panel for 8 seconds until all LEDs momentarily turn off and back on, then release.  
3. (Alternative) Open a browser, go to http://tplinkmodem.net and log in with your admin password.  
4. Navigate to Advanced > System Tools > Backup & Restore and click Factory Restore.  
5. Wait for the router to complete the reset and automatically reboot.

If you have already made a right connection, please contact your ISP to make sure your Internet service is available now.
detailed_results.generated:
The ADSL LED being off indicates the router has failed to synchronize with your DSL line.

1. Verify that the ADSL splitter is properly connected to the phone jack and the modem per the “Connect Your Modem Router” instructions.  
2. Ensure all DSL cables are firmly seated and undamaged, then power-cycle the modem router.  
3. If connections are correct and the LED remains off, contact your ISP to confirm your DSL service is active.

detailed_results.question: What are the possible causes if wireless devices cannot connect to the network?
detailed_results.generated:
The fact that wireless devices can’t join the network usually points to a disabled adapter or service, wrong credentials/configuration, or poor signal/interference.

Solutions:
1. Make sure your device’s wireless function and driver are enabled (on XP, set Wireless Zero Configuration to Automatic and Start in Services).  
2. Confirm you’re entering the correct, case-sensitive Network Security Key (select “use a security key instead of PIN” if prompted).  
3. On the router’s Advanced > Wireless > Wireless Settings page, verify the SSID, Region/Country and ensure “Hide SSID” is off.  
4. If the signal is weak or there’s interference, move closer to the router or switch its channel to 1, 6, or 11.

detailed_results.question: Why might bandwidth control not work as expected?
detailed_results.expected: To use the bandwidth control feature, you’d better set static IP Address on each computer to be controlled or configure Address reservation on the modem router in order to manage easily.
detailed_results.generated:
The issue indicates that your bandwidth control rules aren’t being applied due to misconfigured settings.  
Solutions:  
1. Enable Bandwidth Control under Advanced > Bandwidth Control, choose the correct line type (e.g., DSL), and click Save.  
2. Enter the exact Total Upstream and Downstream bandwidth values from your ISP (1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps) and save.  
3. Set each PC to a static IP or configure Address Reservation on the modem so the rules can match the correct IPs.  
4. For each rule, enter the correct IP Range, specify Upstream/Downstream limits, check “Enable,” and click OK to apply.

detailed_results.question: What is the purpose of IP & MAC Binding feature?
detailed_results.expected: IP & MAC Binding, namely, ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) Binding, is used to bind network device’s IP address to its MAC address. This will prevent ARP spoofing and other ARP attacks by denying network access to an device with matching IP address in the Binding list, but unrecognized MAC address.
detailed_results.generated: IP & MAC Binding binds a network device’s IP address to its MAC address to prevent ARP spoofing and other ARP attacks by denying network access to any device with a matching IP but unrecognized MAC.

detailed_results.question: What is Access Control and how does it differ from MAC Filtering?
detailed_results.expected: Access Control is used to block or allow specific client devices to access your network (via wired or wireless) based on a list of blocked devices (Blacklist) or a list of allowed devices (Whitelist). MAC Filtering exploits the uniqueness of the MAC (Medium Access Control) address, a unique 12-digit hexadecimal address (for example, D8:5D:4C:B4:46:EA) of every network device, to determine if the device can or cannot access your wireless network.
detailed_results.generated: Access Control is used to block or allow specific client devices to access your network (via wired or wireless) based on a list of blocked devices (Blacklist) or a list of allowed devices (Whitelist). It differs from MAC Filtering, which exploits each device’s MAC address solely to determine access to your wireless network.

detailed_results.question: How can you remotely access USB storage connected to the router?
detailed_results.expected: You can access your USB disk outside the local area network. For example: • Share photos and other large files with your friends without logging in to (and paying for) a photo-sharing site or email system. • Get a safe backup for the materials for a presentation. • Remove the files on your camera’s memory card from time to time during the journey.
detailed_results.generated:
1. Insert your USB storage device into the router’s USB port and wait for the USB LED to become solid.  
2. Make sure your router has a public WAN IP (not in the 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x ranges).  
3. Note your router’s WAN IP address (or configured Dynamic DNS domain) and the FTP port number (default is 21).  
4. On a remote computer, open a web browser and enter ftp://<WAN_IP_or_domain>:<port> in the address bar.  
5. Press Enter to connect and download files, or use an FTP client/app to upload files.
